title: Regional tiling & pacing check-in — weekly infra update
content:
Header: Regional tiling & pacing weekly check-in
Date: 2029-02-14
Attendees: Kara Nguyen (owner), Diego Morales, Priya Shah, Ethan Park, Lise Tremblay
---
Purpose: sync on experiments and operational heuristics for region-level GPU tiling (slot bundling) and request pacing (client-routing shaping) to reduce cold-start tail latency while preserving cost targets.
Summary:
- Experimental results from last 7 days (tiling+pacing v0): notable reduction in 99th percentile token latency for long-concat jobs in EU and APAC; overall cold-start events down 38%.
- Cost impact: idle/primed slot spend rose ~6.8% in experiment pool; we measured token-unit cost delta ~+1.2% after accounting for latency-driven throughput gains.
- Risk: edge regions with small instance fleets (sa-east1, sea1) still show noisy preemption; tiling bundle sizes require region-specific tuning.
Key metrics (captured from probe runs, 2029-02-07 -> 2029-02-13):
- us-west1: capacity pool 240 slots, primed=36, average QPS delta +4.1%, cold-starts/day 5 -> 2
- europe-west3: capacity pool 160 slots, primed=28, cold-starts/day 9 -> 3, 99P token latency -46ms
- ap-southeast1: capacity pool 80 slots, primed=12, preemption events 7 -> 6 (no change significant)
Operational notes:
1) Tiling policy update: reduce max-bundle from 8 -> 6 for ap-southeast1 to avoid slot fragmentation; keep 8 in us-west1 for throughput-critical routes.
2) Pacing gate: enable rate-shaping per-customer for customers with >250 concurrent streams to cap burst factor at 1.8x.
3) Prewarm lifecycle: shorten prewarm TTL from 36h -> 18h for spot-backed nodes in SA and APAC; keep 36h in regions with reserved commitments.
4) Fallback routing: add routing rule to prefer dedicated-capacity variants if scheduled latency SLO breach probability > 0.6 in last 10m.
Experiment details:
- Bucketed jobs by sequence-length: short (<512), medium (512-2048), long (>2048). Biggest wins were in long bucket where KV-cache priming reduces token compute spikes.
- Observability: added trace tags tile.bundle_size and pacing.window_ms; dashboard updated under Infra -> Tiling (/confluence link).
Decisions:
- Roll forward tiling+pacing v0 to 40% of traffic in eu-west and 25% in us-west next week (2029-02-21 rollout window).
- Do not expand to APAC until preemption sensitivity test passes threshold (see action 6).
Action items (owner - due):
A1: Diego - implement region-specific bundle cap config and expose as runtime flag (INFRA-3214) - due 2029-02-18
A2: Priya - run 48h cost-sensitivity sim to model spot/primed tradeoffs, include per-token unit economics - due 2029-02-20
A3: Ethan - add telemetry for preemption-correlation with bundle size; instrument preempt_count per-bundle - due 2029-02-17
A4: Kara - schedule canary rollout and incident playbook refresh for tiling/pacing - due 2029-02-19
A5: Lise - coordinate with SRE to create Pager thresholds for routing fallback (probability > 0.6) - due 2029-02-18
A6: Diego & Priya - design APAC preemption-sensitivity stunt (controlled loss injection) and safety rollback plan - due 2029-02-22
Open questions:
- Optimal priming TTLs per cloud provider (GCP vs AWS) — need more data around warmup cost curve beyond 48h.
- Should we add automatic adaptive bundle-sizing algorithm (closed-loop) or keep heuristic thresholds? prototype later in Q2.
Notes/links:
- Experiment dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/tiling-pacing-v0
- Runbook draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/58
- Related Jira: INFRA-3214, INFRA-3242 (routing fallback), COST-97
Retrospective snippet:
- What worked: focused telemetry made regression detection quick; bundling reduced tail latency as hypothesized.
- What failed: initial APAC bundles caused fragmentation because instance types returned variable slot counts; fixed by enforcing min-alignment.
Next meeting: weekly sync on 2029-02-21 10:00 PT; agenda: canary rollout readiness, cost sim results, APAC stunt design.

Notes to self: keep clear rollback thresholds (latency + cost) and ensure PDs are pre-notified.
